complaint: We queued push notifications for a donation campaign last week and as far as we can tell none of them ever went out. No errors on our side — we got 202s back.

response.restated_complaint: The engineer queued push notifications for a campaign and, despite receiving 202 acknowledgements from the ingest API, none of the push messages were actually delivered, with no errors visible on their side.

hypotheses.summary: All 4 accepted push messages in the window stopped after 'publish to topic' in comms-ingest and never produced any downstream span in comms-orchestrator or comms-sender — they were accepted (202) but silently dropped on the hop out of ingest, before the orchestrator ever ran. This is not tied to one tenant or one day (3 tenants, 4 days), matching a systemic push-channel problem rather than a one-off campaign issue. The two competing explanations the data can't distinguish are: (1) a topic subscription filter policy that doesn't match 'push', silently discarding the message after successful publish, or (2) no queue/consumer exists for 'push' at all.
hypotheses.why_this_rank: This finding directly matches the complaint: push messages accepted (202) but never reaching a provider, with 4/4 push messages affected and 0 downstream spans.

hypotheses.summary: The reason no errors were visible on the engineer's side: every one of 273 spans reports status OK and 0 of 2820 log records are at ERROR, even for the exact 4 messages that never reached a provider. A dropped message produces no error signal at all — only an absence of downstream spans — so any dashboard or alert built on span status or log level would show this pipeline as fully healthy throughout the incident.
hypotheses.why_this_rank: Explains the 'no errors on our side' part of the complaint — it's a separate, corroborating finding about observability blind spots rather than the root cause of the drop itself.

ruled_out.claim: The duplicate-delivery issue (D2) is causing the missing push notifications.
ruled_out.why_not: D2 affects 3 messages, all attributable to queue redelivery on the sender side after a successful send; none are push channel messages, and duplication implies over-delivery, not loss.

ruled_out.claim: SMS trace context loss (D4) or provider throttling (D3.provider_degradation.email) explain the push failure.
ruled_out.why_not: D4 is scoped entirely to the sms channel (8/8 sms messages) and D3 is scoped entirely to email (6 email sends); neither affects push messages.

would_resolve: the topic's subscription filter policy for message_type=push
the queue list and redrive/DLQ policy for the push channel
whether the 4 lost push messages are recoverable from a dead-letter queue
